payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_spec_citations.py::test_a_citation_whose_construct_sits_at_one_span_is_rewritten_to_that_span stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'Rewrites returned in defect-kind order or reversed, not text order.' applied to saffron/spec_citations.py as an edit. The claim was "`rewrite_moved_citations(text, defects, held)` rewrites each defect whose citation's offset `held` maps to a name, when that name opens exactly one span in the defect. That citation's range in `text` becomes the span, written `S` for one line and `S-E` otherwise. Its path, or its bare form, and every other character stay as written. It returns the new text, one rewrite per such defect in text order, and the defects left. Each rewrite names the path, the old range and the new range. The witness drives a path citation and a bare one, each as a single line and as a range. It drives a new span of one line and one of several. It drives two rewrites of different lengths in one sentence, and a paragraph wrapped over two lines. It drives one citation text written twice, judged right once and moved once. Checked again at the same commit, the new text reports no defect.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
